predecessors.name: Pala Empire
predecessors.text: Rarh (Radha), where the Senas were Pala sāmantas

successors.name: Deva dynasty
successors.text: southeastern Bengal, the last Sena land

successors.name: Ghurid dynasty
successors.text: Nadia, Gauda and Lakhnauti, taken by Bakhtiyar Khalji in 1203-1204 for the Ghurids (infobox: 'Ghurid conquest of Bengal: 1205')

ledger.x: 1070: the Sena family enters Pala service in Rarh.
1070: Rarh is held under the Palas.
1095: Hemanta Sena 'usurped power and styled himself king in 1095 AD'; the Vijaya Sena page adds that Vijaya Sena 'obtained an independent position in Rarh in recognition of his help to Ramapala'.

c. 1152: Vijayasena ousts the Varmans from southeastern Bengal. 'So it seems probable that Vijaya Sena ousted the Varmans from southeastern Bengal in the middle of the 12th century AD'. The Sena page has Vaṅga only 'by the end of' his reign (1159); the Barrackpur plate was 'issued from…
1159: Ballala Sena 'made Nadia the capital as well': the court is at Nadia (Nabadwip) beside Vikramapura, which the Vijaya Sena page names ('He had capital in Vijayapuri and Vikramapura').
1169: the Pala land of Bihar passes to the Senas.
1204: the court withdraws to southeastern Bengal.
1230: the Sena kingdom ends in southeastern Bengal.

wars.name: Sena conquest of the Pala and Varman lands
wars.outcome: The Senas oust the Varmans from southeastern Bengal c.

wars.name: Sena-Gahadavala conflicts
wars.outcome: Infobox only ('Sena-Gahadavala conflicts: 1155-1206'); the Lakshmana Sena page has him campaign against Varanasi, then under Jayachandra, and counts Kashi in his peak empire, undated.

wars.name: Khalji conquest of Bengal
wars.outcome: Bakhtiyar Khalji 'subjugated much of Bihar in 1200', captured Nadia in 1203-1204 by surprise ('The old Sena king, who was then at his dinner, was completely taken by surprise'), took Gauda and made Lakhnauti the seat of government; Lakshmana Sena withdrew to…

certainty.note: Every Sena frontier is soft: the pages name regions (Rarh, Vanga, Varendra, Gaur, Nadia) and no boundary or treaty line.
